tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
- Allows Claude to search the web and use the results to inform responses
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Returns search result information formatted as search result blocks, including links as markdown hyperlinks
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond Claude's knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - You MUST follow this:
  - After answering the user's question, you MUST include a "Sources:" section at the end of your response
  - In the Sources section, list all relevant URLs from the search results as markdown hyperlinks: [Title](URL)
  - This is MANDATORY - never skip including sources in your response
  - Example format:

    [Your answer here]

    Sources:
    - [Source Title 1](https://example.com/1)
    - [Source Title 2](https://example.com/2)

Usage notes:
  - Domain filtering is supported to include or block specific websites
  - Web search is only available in the US

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
  - The current month is October 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
  - Example: If the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation" with the current year, NOT last year

- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

content.thinking:
OPA runs `run --server --addr=0.0.0.0:8181` with no `--authentication=token` and no decision logging restrictions. By default OPA's server exposes the full REST API including policy management (PUT /v1/policies) to anyone who can reach it. It's on the `backend` compose network only (not published to host — no ports: section), so exposure is limited to other containers on the backend network. In Kubernetes (helm), check how OPA is deployed — likely a sidecar. Finding: Minor/Important — OPA decision endpoint and admin API unauthenticated within cluster network; lateral-movement attacker in backend network could PUT a permissive policy (`allow := true`) and then... actually wait — if attacker can reach OPA they could rewrite policy so that OPA allows everything; but app-level ROLE_ACTIONS check happens before OPA and independently denies. So overriding OPA only removes the defense-in-depth layer, doesn't grant access alone. Still worth Minor finding: unauthenticated OPA admin API on shared backend network; remediation: `--authentication=token` or restrict to decision API only (`--addr` + `opa run --server` doesn't separate; can use `--authentication=token`, or move to sidecar with localhost binding).

@router.post(
    "/assets/{asset_id}/actions",
    response_model=NetworkActionResponse,
    responses=STANDARD_ERROR_RESPONSES,
    summary="Queue a configuration change for an edge device",
)
async def queue_network_action(
    request: Request,
    asset_id: str,
    body: Annotated[NetworkActionRequest, Body()],
    identity: Annotated[IdentityContext, Depends(get_identity)],
    authorizer: Annotated[Authorizer, Depends(get_authorizer)],
    service: Annotated[NetworkAssuranceService, Depends(get_network_assurance_service)],
) -> NetworkActionResponse:
    """Queue a change; the device applies and re-validates it on next upload.

    Deliberately *not* forwarded to the device here. The edge owns a
    parameter whitelist with range checks, and it is the only party that can
    observe whether a change took effect. The server records intent; the
    device records outcome.
    """

    authorizer.require(
        identity,
        Action.MANAGE_NETWORK_DEVICE,
        ResourceContext(identity.tenant_id, resource_id=asset_id),
        request_id=getattr(request.state, "request_id", "unavailable"),
    )
    try:
        action_id = service.queue_action(
            identity.tenant_context,
            asset_id,
            config_key=body.config_key,
            config_value=body.config_value,
            issued_by=identity.subject_id,
        )
    except NetworkAssuranceNotFound as exc:
        raise _not_found(asset_id) from exc

content.thinking:
All confirmed. The applyPendingActions chain: dedup by action_id, generation fail-closed for trialable/v2, stale check. Non-triable keys without v2 metadata skip generation gates — this is by design "direct channel" but combined with unauthenticated response it means an on-path attacker on the HTTP channel can push non-triable config keys (e.g., active_probe.targets, rtt.target strings, bpf_obj path, server.data_dir) without generation protection. Wait — is active_probe.targets trialable? Summary said trialableKeyNames excludes identity keys, enabled flags, bpf_obj, active_probe.* — so active_probe.* is NOT trialable → direct channel → no generation gate. Also does queue_action on cloud side always attach generation? Cloud queue_action generates generation (max+1) always — so legitimately issued actions have generation → v2_metadata present → gates apply. The gates only fail for actions lacking generation AND claim_token AND nonce — i.e., crafted by someone who knows protocol shape. An on-path attacker who forges a response body with crafted actions (no metadata) could apply direct-channel keys (non-triable ones) with generation=0 bypass. But wait — direct-channel application also calls setMonitorParam which does its own whitelist/range validation via weaknet_dbus::setMonitorParam. So attacker impact: any config key accepted by setMonitorParam that is non-triable — active_probe.targets, rtt.target, server.data_dir, bpf_obj path? Let me not overclaim; setMonitorParam validates via applyMonitorParam. From summary: "active_probe.targets, *.bpf_obj, server.data_dir accept arbitrary strings". So an MITM on the response channel can change probe targets (data-plane redirection — telemetry probing attacker-chosen hosts), bpf_obj path (loads arbitrary BPF object path? if it accepts arbitrary path and loading happens... could load attacker-controlled .o if they can also place a file — they can't remotely place files, but path could point to /tmp/... placed by local attacker), data_dir (SQLite path → could redirect DB to arbitrary location). Severity: Important, conditional on channel exposure (default config uses loopback http via tunnel — mitigates in current deployment).

Actually one more check: is the response channel the same TLS-protected POST? postSigned sends to edge.url; response is whatever the server returns over that same connection. If edge.url were https, response would be TLS-authenticated to the server (but still no signature — TLS server auth covers it). Over http (current default), no protection at all. So finding: response path integrity depends entirely on transport; default config is plaintext loopback.

Also X-Edge-Token in headers over plaintext http — but loopback only in default config. Deployment via ssh tunnel (per memory) keeps it on loopback. So the "Important" finding should be framed as: "if edge.url is ever switched to a non-loopback URL without TLS (config accepts any URL; nothing enforces https), token+body are plaintext and responses are forgeable" — configuration-level risk with no code guardrail (no https enforcement in code). That's fair as Important/conditional.

# 全仓库安全评审报告（安全维度）

评审范围：边缘端（server/、tools/）、云端（Large-Model-Application/）、仓库凭据卫生与 git 历史。全程只读；未修改任何文件。

---

## 发现（按严重度排序）

### [Important] 1. 板端上行响应通道无完整性校验，且代码层不强制 HTTPS——配置下发可被链路上攻击者伪造

- **证据**：
  - `/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/server/src/edge_telemetry_exporter.cpp:641-753` — `applyPendingActions(response_body)` 直接解析并执行 HTTP 响应体中的 `pending_actions`，**响应体没有任何签名校验**（对比上行方向有完整 Ed25519 detached signature，`:502,552-567`）。
  - `/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/server/src/weaknet_config.cpp:467` — `edge.url` 接受任意 scheme，加载时无 https 强制；`config.yaml` 默认 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/...`（当前 ssh 反向隧道部署下是回环，构成实际缓解）。
  - `edge_telemetry_exporter.cpp:565` — `X-Edge-Token` 作为明文 HTTP 头发送；`edge.url` 一旦改成非回环地址，预共享令牌与全部遥测内容明文过网。
  - `edge_telemetry_exporter.cpp:655-670` — generation 门禁只对“trialable 键或带 v2 元数据（generation/nonce/claim_token）”的动作 fail-closed；**三个元数据全缺的伪造动作绕过 generation 检查**，落入 direct-channel 路径。
- **攻击场景**：`edge.url` 若被配置为非回环 http 地址（代码不阻止），链路上（同网段 ARP/DNS 劫持、被控网关）攻击者可：(a) 嗅探 `X-Edge-Token` 与全部诊断数据；(b) 伪造遥测 POST 的响应体，注入不带 v2 元数据的动作，直接改写非 trialable 键（`active_probe.*` 探测目标、`rtt.target`、`*.bpf_obj` 路径、`server.data_dir`，见 `weaknet_config.cpp:692-855` 的 direct-channel 白名单外沿）。运行时 setter 仍拒绝 `edge.url/token/tenant/device_id`（`weaknet_config.cpp:823-855`，注释明确），故无法顶替设备身份，但可把探针重定向到攻击者选择的目标、篡改探测语义。
- **缓解因素**：当前部署走 `127.0.0.1` 回环隧道，实际暴露面为零；identity 键不可远程改写。
- **修复方向**：(a) 云端对 `pending_actions` 也做 Ed25519 签名（与上行对称）；(b) 配置加载时对非回环 `edge.url` 强制 https 或直接拒绝；(c) 要求**所有**远程动作必须携带 generation（v2 元数据），缺则拒绝，而不是仅对 trialable 键要求。

### [Important] 2. 云端直连下发接口 `POST /network/assets/{asset_id}/actions` 完全绕过 council/approval/catalog 流水线

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/Large-Model-Application/src/industrial_ops_agent/api/routes/network_assurance.py:515-552` — 仅要求 `Action.MANAGE_NETWORK_DEVICE` + 租户隔离，然后直接 `service.queue_action(config_key, config_value)`；无 council 提案、无审批绑定、无服务端 catalog 白名单校验（docstring 自述“设备端复验”是唯一防线）。
- **攻击场景**：被攻陷或恶意的运维账号（持有 MANAGE_NETWORK_DEVICE 角色）可跳过全部人工审批链，向任意本租户设备队列推送任意键值；结合发现 1 的 direct-channel 路径，非 trialable 键在板端不经 TRIAL/回滚机制直接生效。该路径对 LLM 不可达（见下文“已证防护充分”第 7 条），属人/API 面风险。
- **修复方向**：对非 trialable 键强制走 approval 流程（复用 `network_action_approval.py` 链），或至少在服务端按 `edge_action_catalog.py` 校验 config_key，并要求 `EXECUTE_NETWORK_ACTION` 而非仅 MANAGE。

### [Minor] 3. `EXECUTE_NETWORK_ACTION` 未纳入 OPA 强制集合（纵深防御缺口）

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/Large-Model-Application/src/industrial_ops_agent/auth/policy.py:695-751` — `OPA_ENFORCED_ACTIONS` 含 `EXECUTE_ACTION`、`MANAGE_NETWORK_DEVICE`、`PROPOSE_ACTION`、`APPROVE_ACTION` 等，但不含 `network_action.execute`（枚举定义 `:183`，角色授权 `:322,398`）。最敏感的远程执行动作反而跳过了外部策略引擎。
- **影响**：绕过 OPA 层仅剩角色+SoD+绑定校验（这三层是真实的），但少了一层独立裁决。
- **修复**：把 `Action.EXECUTE_NETWORK_ACTION` 加入 `OPA_ENFORCED_ACTIONS`（OPA 不可用时按现有逻辑 fail-closed 503）。

### [Minor] 4. OPA 服务端无认证监听，位于共享 backend 网络

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/Large-Model-Application/compose.lite.yaml:300` — `command: ["run","--server","--addr=0.0.0.0:8181",...]`，无 `--authentication=token`；客户端 `config.py:124` 默认 `http://opa:8181`。OPA 默认 REST API 含策略管理端点（`PUT /v1/policies`）。
- **场景**：backend 网络内被攻陷的任意容器可改写 authz 策略为 `allow:=true`，抹掉 OPA 这层纵深防御（应用内 `ROLE_ACTIONS` 检查独立于此，仍生效）。
- **修复**：`opa run --server --authentication=token`（或 mTLS），或以 sidecar 形式仅绑定 localhost；compose 中未向宿主发布端口，横向面已有缓解。

### [Minor] 5. `tools/ci.sh` 部署令牌进入进程 argv + /tmp 短暂可读窗口

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/tools/ci.sh:209-212` — `EDGE_TOKEN` 被插值进远程 shell 命令字符串（本地与板端 `ps` 在部署窗口内可见令牌）；`:211-220` 板端 `/tmp/weaknet-config.yaml` 在 scp（radxa 属主）到 `chmod 600 /etc/weaknet/config.yaml`（`:220`）之间存在默认权限可读窗口。令牌从不回显到报告/日志（已确认），字符集校验 `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`（`:210`）限制了注入面。
- **修复**：令牌经 stdin/独立文件传递（`ssh ... 'sudo tee ...'` + fd），板端先 `install -m600` 再写入，避免出现在 argv。

### [Minor] 6. compose 本地默认口令（明确标注 local，但存在误用风险）

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/Large-Model-Application/compose.observability.yaml:110`（Grafana `industrial-ops-local`）；`compose.integration.yaml:26,90-96`（Neo4j `local-graphrag-password`）、`:485`（Label Studio `m3-label-studio-local-password`）、`:529`（Marquez `marquez`）；`compose.realtime.yaml:4,48`（TURN `local-realtime-turn-secret-change-before-shared-use`）；`compose.lite.yaml:196`（`disabled-local-a2a-secret`）。
- **缓解**：生产关键凭据全部 `:?` fail-fast（`compose.lite.yaml:123,152,190`）；dev_lite 用 `secrets.token_urlsafe` 生成随机口令写入 gitignored 的 `.env.m1.local`（`scripts/dev_lite.sh:46-77`，`Large-Model-Application/.gitignore:20` 已 `git check-ignore` 验证）。
- **修复**：文档化“这些值仅限本机 compose”；Grafana/Marquez 建议同样改为环境变量必填。

### [Minor] 7. TRIAL 看门狗把 UNKNOWN 计为健康

- **证据**：`/home/ubuntu/个人学习/AI-powered-Network-Diagnostics/server/src/edge_telemetry_exporter.cpp:848-849` — `healthy = (overall != BAD) && (reach != BAD)`，UNKNOWN 与 GOOD 同等待遇，超时后直接 `confirmStable`。
- **影响**：配置变更后若健康状态因证据不足回落为 UNKNOWN，可能把未证实无害的变更确认为 STABLE。无快照场景已正确 fail-safe 回滚（`:834-844`），部分抵消。

## 已核查且防护充分的区域（覆盖性清单）

**边缘端**
1. **D-Bus root 门禁完整性**：所有改变状态的方法均有 `requireRootCaller`——`ExecuteAction`（`server/src/dbus_service.cpp:566`）、`Ping`（`:695`）、`SetMonitorParam`（`:1760`，TRIAL 期间另拒本地写 `:1790-1798`）、enable/disable/restart（`:1978`）、`SaveMonitorOverrides`（`:2022`）；其余方法只读。`requireRootCaller` fail-closed（`:531-557`，`dbus_bus_get_unix_user` 失败即拒）。系统总线策略 `tools/com.example.WeakNet.conf:8-16`：root 独占 own，default 上下文仅允许调用本服务接口——由于逐方法 UID 门禁完备，该放权是有意且安全的。

---

**总结**：无 Critical 级发现。核心防护（D-Bus 门禁、命令注入面、签名上行、租户 RLS、审批绑定、LLM 工具治理、凭据卫生）经代码逐条验证属实，不是文档姿态。两个 Important 项都指向同一条设计轴——**下行/响应方向的信任模型弱于上行方向**：板端无条件执行云端响应（发现 1），云端又留了一条不经审批的直连下发口（发现 2）；两者叠加时，链路攻击者或持角色的恶意调用者可改动板端探测语义。建议优先补齐响应签名与直连口审批这两个闭环。
